To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) SEs are able to train RL agents that are able to solve real environments, and 2) RNs are able to replace rewards in real environments, and thus can be used for reward engineering
we propose to train RL agents using proxy models of the real environments that are represented by neural networks and can be learned via bi-level optimization.

(a) we introduce a novel concept of SEs and RN proxies for training RL agents, (b) these SE proxies allow us (i) to learn agents without interacting with the real environment and (ii) to train new agents faster, (c) we show that the proxies are robust to hyperparameter variation, and (d) we demonstrate that these proxies can transfer to unseen agents

the question of whether RL agents can learn to solve tasks in real environments without any interactions with them.

the following questions: Can we train RL agents on a proxy environment model? How can we learn a proxy model that is a better teacher for RL than the real environment? How can we transfer the proxy model to new RL algorithms?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work provides a novel and effective approach to train RL agents on real environments without any interactions.
our approach can reduce the number of real interactions by a factor of 2-5 while maintaining the same task performance.
the proposed method is a novel approach to transfer learning in the field of reinforcement learning and it is able to transfer knowledge from a source environment to a target environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our proposed new concept of SEs and RN can help RL agents to learn better policies with fewer interactions in the real environment.
SEs and RN proxies can be used to reduce the number of interactions with the real environments for training RL agents.

SEs and RN are useful tools for RL training and can significantly speed up training and improve sample efficiency.
